newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Yanjing Beer to issue A shares in June.
newsitem.headline: China's Yanjing Beer to issue A shares in June.

text.p: China's biggest brewer Yanjing Beer Group Co has won approval to issue 72 million domestic currency A shares in Shenzhen, the Beijing Economic Daily said on Saturday.
The issue was scheduled for June 6 and was expected to raise 570 million yuan ($68.7 million) for the group's Yanjing Beer Shareholding Co, the newspaper said. Shares were priced at 7.34 yuan each.
Beijing Securities Co would be the main underwriter for the issue, the newspaper said.
The brewer would use the funds raised from the share issue to raise beer output by 150,000 tonnes a year, add a mineral water operation and carry out technical renovations, it said.
Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd, which debuted last week on the Hong Kong bourse to overwhelming response, has a stake in the brewery.
Yanjing Beer Shareholding is partly owned by Beijing Xidan Market Co Ltd.
Yanjing controls 85 percent of the Beijing beer market and brewed 571,000 tonnes of beer last year, up 68.2 percent from 1995, earlier figures show.
The firm's pre-tax profits last year soared 58.2 percent from 1995 to 357.99 million yuan.
